summary: Guests can send absolute-form HTTP requests to different hosts
description:
### Summary

Wasmtime's implementation of `wasi:http` in the `wasmtime-wasi-http` crate did not check that the value a guest passes to `set-path-with-query` on an outgoing request is actually a path. Absolute-form values such as `http://other.example/x` were accepted and written verbatim as the request target of the HTTP/1.1 request line, while the connection and the `Host` header used the authority the guest set with `set-authority`:

```
GET http://other.example/x HTTP/1.1
host: allowed.example
```

Wasmtime only connects to the authority the guest set, and any sort of request filtering based on host is done by the authority the guest set as well. However, RFC 9112 requires a server receiving an absolute-form target to ignore `Host`, so if the allowed authority is a forward proxy or a gateway that honors absolute-form targets, it forwards the request to `other.example`. A guest may then reach hosts the embedder did not have visibility into or allow. Both `wasi:http@0.2` and `wasi:http@0.3` are affected, including guests run with `wasmtime serve` and `wasmtime run -S http`.

### Impact

This issue can cause hosts using the `wasmtime-wasi-http` crate to erroneously have requests sent to hosts that are otherwise explicitly disallowed in filtering policies.

### Patches

Wasmtime 36.0.18, 48.0.6, and 49.0.3 have all been released which fixes this issue.
